verdict.rationale: Nitrokey documents that the Nitrokey 3 includes a 'Common Criteria EAL 6+ certified secure element'. That covers the certification half of the story, but only at the chip level, not as a certified device model. The pack has no FIPS 140 validation and no documented water or crush resistance; one community user also describes the U2F key as feeling flimsy. Missing for 10: device-level FIPS 140 or Common Criteria certification, documented water/crush durability ratings, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, certified models exist for regulated environments — FIPS 140 validated or Common Criteria certified — with documented durability (water/crush resistance)

citations.quote: Common Criteria EAL 6+ certified secure element
